title: sizeof(pointer) silently wipes less than intended
root_cause: Inside wipe(), buf is a function parameter -- a pointer -- so sizeof(buf) is the size of a pointer (commonly 8 bytes on 64-bit systems), not the size of the array the caller passed in. No crash happens; the bug is silent.
defenses: Never use sizeof on a pointer parameter to mean "the size of what it points to".
Pass the real capacity explicitly as a separate parameter.
Use -Wsizeof-pointer-memaccess (part of -Wall) to catch this pattern at compile time.
For secrets specifically, use explicit_bzero or memset_s, which also resist compiler removal.
